answer: As the cryptographic dawn approaches post-quantum standards, a rigorous architecture enforces solvent staking via super-linear capital expenditure and zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions, applying quadratic slashing to petrify the brittle shale of unconsolidated low-value nodes. We quantify the precise economic delta between punitive penalties and collateralized risks to demonstrate a robust Nash equilibrium backed by negative expected utility, calculating that the marginal cost of attack must exceed the potential extraction value to sustain consensus against grouped adversaries.
